Dialogs.Dialog: Anegasaki

Hey, do you put sauce
on your curry rice？

I hear about it sometimes...
Did a customer do that？

Yeah... I thought it was
a little strange.

Maybe it makes it sweeter.
Well, to each their own.
Some put mayo on sashimi.

That might not be so weird.
I mean, it's kind of like
carpaccio, right？

Carpaccio... That's
French food, right？

Italian. It's usually beef,
but they use raw fish
a lot, too.
You eat it with mayo？

Mayonnaise sauce. So mayo
itself probably goes well
with sashimi.

I don't know about ●,
but I prefer soy sauce
with sashimi.
Hehe, me too.

Putting sauce on curry rice
used to be normal, apparently.
Anegasaki

Really？ How long ago
is 'used to be'？

Huh, I wonder. Aren't you
more familiar with this
kind of thing, ▲姉ヶ崎＊▲？

Are you calling me
an old lady？

We're only one year apart!
I mean, like in old movies.

Movies... Now that you
mention it... didn't they
do that in Graveyard on
Third Street？

When did that movie
come out？

About 40 years ago,
I think.

See, you really do know
a lot about the past.

I'm not sure if that's
actually a compliment...
Anegasaki

Sauce on curry might not be
that surprising. I mean,
there's coffee on frappes.

Frappes... Coffee on
shaved ice？ Wouldn't
the ice melt？

Not hot coffee, it's made
into a syrup... Come on,
you know what I mean.

So it's like frozen iced
coffee. If it were shaved ice,
what would ● put on it？

Hehe, all kids love
strawberry syrup, right？

Yeah？ Then I guess putting
soy sauce on it makes
you an adult.

Soy sauce on a frappe？
Hehe.
Or sauce？
Hehe, jeez.

We talked about shaved ice
before, but what kind of
syrup does ▲姉ヶ崎＊▲ like？
Anegasaki

Hehe, what do you think？
It's not strawberry.

Lemon, melon, green apple,
grapefruit, pineapple,
blueberry, matcha...
What else is there？

Just guessing everything？
Too bad, they're all wrong.

Orange, ramune... I've said
all the common and rare ones.
I give up.
Condensed milk.

Ah, I forgot about that!
But wait, isn't that...

What, you got a problem
with that？

Isn't that more childish
than strawberry？
Hehe, I just like it.
Anegasaki
You know how animals have camouflage？
Yeah, the stuff that lets them blend in.
What about pandas？
Pandas...
I wonder what that black and white pattern mimics？
Black and white... what is it？ Is there a place like that... Oh, zebras are black and white too.
Those stripes act as camouflage when they're between trees.
So pandas too？
They don't have stripes, so I don't think that's it.
Then what could it be？
Anegasaki
I just thought of something that looks like a panda's pattern.
Oh, what does that black and white mimic？
Onigiri.
The kind with seaweed just on the bottom. The standard convenience store type, you know？
...I get what you mean, but.
Don't pandas look like onigiri from a distance？
But if they look like onigiri, wouldn't they be targeted more... I mean, it's food.
The ones targeting them would be carnivores, so they wouldn't eat onigiri, right？
Pandas are only in China, and onigiri are Japanese... I'm getting confused.
Anegasaki
I thought of something else that looks like a panda's pattern.
Other than onigiri？
Yeah, a police car.
Haha. I don't even know what's going on anymore.
Even poachers wouldn't go near a police car, right？
Um, are police cars in China two-tone black and white too？
I don't know about that.
Isn't your research a bit lacking？ You fail! Just kidding.
Eh！？
Anegasaki
There's a horror movie called '47 Pandas: The Cursed Raid'.
Unreleased, of course.
You guessed it. In the movie, pandas come marching through the snow...
That must be the raid scene.
Right. The white parts blend in with the snow, and the black parts look like shadows... so no one notices.
That theory is more convincing than onigiri or police cars.
Yeah. I think that's how black and white camouflage works. Movies can be helpful, huh？
Yeah, very helpful. By the way, where are the pandas raiding？
The Shinsengumi.
(...That movie really isn't helpful at all.)
Anegasaki
Hey, why are greengrocers called 'yaoya'？
Why... what do you mean？
Why not just call them 'vegetable shops' or 'fruit shops'？
Fish is at a 'fish shop', meat is at a 'meat shop'. But 'yaoya'... why is that？
Because there are 800 kinds？ Of fruits and vegetables, I mean.
If we're talking numbers, there's a lot of fish, too. Meat seems countable, though.
Beef, pork, chicken, and mutton... Even with horse and boar, it's countable.
I saw kangaroo meat at the supermarket the other day.
Kangaroo？ People eat that？
Seems like it.
All animal lives are equal, of course, but... It's still a bit shocking.
Did you figure out why they're called 'yaoya' like we talked about？
Anegasaki
I was thinking about it. Veggies have been close to Japanese people for ages.
I think that's true anywhere in the world...
Especially for Japanese！ We're a farming people.
Well... I guess so.
The close bond with veggies, becoming one with our lives, creates worldly desires...
...Worldly desires？
So they made it the same number to drive them away. Like the New Year's bell.
Aren't there 800 worldly desires？
Hehehe？
(She got it wrong...)
Anegasaki
About the 'yaoya' thing.
It's not worldly desires.
Jeez, forget about that. I think it has to do with the benefits of vegetables.
Benefits... Sounds like a hot spring.
Vitamin C, Vitamin A... There are 800 benefits like nutrition and diet effects.
And that makes it a 'yaoya'？
Yep.
...You think so？
Anegasaki
About the 'yaoya' thing.
Ah, the origin of the name？
I think it comes from 'yaoyorozu'—the 8 million.
...The number of gods？
Right. Basically, it just means there's a whole lot of them.
Hmm, that sounds plausible. Should we look it up and see if you're right？
We could... but that'd be boring.
Is that how it is？
That's how it is. It's fun to think about these things together with you.
Anegasaki
Towano is sister cities with somewhere else, right？
I've heard that. What country was it again？ Somewhere in Europe...
I wonder why they're called "sister cities"？
Is it because they get along well？
If that were it, they could just be "best friend cities."
Because the cities are similar？ Like in size, environment, or eco policies.
That might be it. But why "sisters"？
Why？
Why aren't they brother cities？
...I wonder why. One of the Seven Wonders of the World？
Hehe, who knows？
Anegasaki
Oh right, about the "sister" part of sister cities...
Ah, the Seven Wonders of the World.
No. I think they use "sisters" because that's the global standard.
Standard？
You know, all the great world masterpieces are about "sisters."
Are they？
Like "Little Hay."
What else？
And the painting of the sisters by Norenoir.
Hmm.
For those reasons, "sisters" is the global standard.
(For a standard, she only has two examples...)
You said before that all the great world masterpieces are about "sisters," right？
Anegasaki
Yeah.
What about "The Brothers Fyodor"？
Hehe, you got so defensive. You actually looked it up.
I'm on the library committee, after all.
But the brothers in that story don't get along. It's so heavy and dark.
Do you really think cities would say, "Let's be like those brothers"？
...Probably not.
Wouldn't it be exciting to be invited to be sisters like in "Little Hay"？
True... wait, is that really the issue here？
Typhoons are named after women.
Anegasaki
What do you mean？
The sister cities thing. It reminded me that typhoons are women too.
Oh, hurricane names.
Like Susie, Katrina, or an angry ▲姉ヶ崎＊▲.
That last one isn't real.
Haha, well, you know. I guess women just fit better for these things than men.
Maybe that's just because you're a boy？
Is that so？
Boys all love cute girls, don't they？
I guess. I like ●, too.
Hmm...
Like ▲姉ヶ崎＊▲.
Oh, you dummy.
